idiom_name: widget-constructor wrapper over function pointers, or a toolkit composite-widget subclass
implementation_notes: C has no component value: a GTK widget is a struct pointer with a class vtable managed by the toolkit (Gtk.Widget is documented as the base class of all widgets), so there is no component type to wrap and no way to return a new component. The nearest realization wraps the constructor instead - a function that takes a widget-constructor function pointer and returns a constructor - which is a higher-order function over functions rather than over components, and every widget family needs its own wrapper. Because the pattern's leverage (one enhancer reused across many components without editing each) is not expressible, prefer a GObject composite-widget template subclass or a constructor wrapper for the concrete widget family, keeping the enhancement at that family's constructor boundary.
pitfalls: A widget pointer carries no type information, so the wrapper cannot preserve the wrapped widget's class contract; callers must know which widget family it holds.
Ownership is manual (g_object_ref/g_object_unref): a wrapper that returns a widget without transferring ownership either leaks it or leaves it dangling.
Toolkit instance data and signal handlers are set per widget class, so an enhancement written in the constructor wrapper can be bypassed by any code that constructs the widget another way.
alternative: A GObject composite-widget template subclass for the concrete widget family, or a constructor-wrapping function over function pointers - the enhancement is defined inside that family and is not reusable across components.
